question: When the inspectors move inside CodeMother, do the builders' gates reach them through a client tool she publishes (a), over the bus at each crossing (b), or some other way?
why_it_blocks: Once build_inspector, diagnostic_inspector and corrosion move inside CodeMother, RULE 1 reds every caller outside her: the emit chokepoint (cairn/tools/base/transitions.py, every crossing), tools/base/validation.py, tools/chain/grammar.py, tools/base/breadcrumb_log.py, tools/gate/gate.py, and the tester device (devices/tester/hollow.py). Options: (a) she publishes the gate functions as her client tool (RULE 1 already allows 'plus any client tool it publishes'; charter published_by_device: true) and the chokepoint keeps calling them in-process; (b) the chokepoint asks her over the bus at each crossing, so no ticket crosses while her process is down (adversarial by construction, but she sits on every crossing's critical path). CC's lean: (a), because the chokepoint calling her gate IS the builder passing through her gate, and it adds no runtime dependency.
answer: but why would she call her gates? that's what becomes the question, and the answer is you have her managing something that doesn't need managing. first if all, obviously, our parts have to be able to work on themselves. this causes problems sometimes which is why testing things are marked as such and we just demand that the system can tolerate and igore them. so that's a part. next part: what is an inspector/gate? its a thing that a ticket asks if it can pass. deterministic code says i'm ready for this gate! hey gate, can i pass? deterministic code says 'lets take a look' and the deterministic inspector runs his inspection(s) over the artifacts in question. could be a ticket, could be code, could launch additional scripts and checking tools to complete it's work. then it issues a finding. then that finding is the key that unlocks the gate, and the gate gets the thing certified. that certification being completed is an event. that event triggers probes for any device in the system that can handle that event. TICKETME, BUILDME, WATCHME, PROVEME will all have eventually their own handlers that will recieve that event's notification. over the bus. no orchestrator, everything happens automatically as a result of their being appropriate handlers. if two of something try and pick up a specific ticket, then we have to adjudicate that in some way. but for sure, it hasn't happened yet, so i haven't worried about it yet.
